rubrics.justification: Generally matches the provided 0DD assessment by identifying poor expansion, absent/degenerative ICM, and poor TE, but adds uncertain image-specific details (collapse artifact, debris, borderline C/D) that are not clearly supported.
Integrates age, FSH, semen quality, tubal factor, prior biochemical pregnancies, endometrial thickness, and lifestyle reasonably well, though AMH is unavailable and BMI is not meaningfully discussed.

Reasoning is mostly logical and consistent: favorable patient factors are weighed against very poor embryo morphology. Minor issues include speculative emphasis on hydrosalpinx and some internal hedging around exact prognosis.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice and Gardner grading interpretation, including cautious prognosis, SET, luteal support, and considering hydrosalpinx treatment. Slight overreach/speculation around PGT-A and hydrosalpinx prevents a top score.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future cycles, including SET, review of tubal status, embryology history, and possible further workup. Useful but not highly tailored beyond standard considerations.
